mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a single month leads to a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to compressed credit spreads and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the same month of the rate hike (t-test p > 0.05), or credit spread proxies (e.g., BAMLH0A0HYM2) show no widening.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims exceeding 200,000 for two consecutive months coincides with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive during the identified labor weakness period (t-test p < 0.05), or alternative labor proxies (e.g., UNRATE) show no significant decline.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows faster than consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over a 2-month window, it signals supply-side strength that supports higher S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate over the previous 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the supply signal (Rank IC < 0.05), or alternative demand proxies (e.g., HOUST) contradict the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in residential housing starts (HOUST) below 1.0 million units for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as market anticipates softening construction activity and consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative during the contraction (t-test p > 0.05), or alternative housing proxies (e.g., building permits) show no significant decline.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for the first time in three months during a tightening cycle, it triggers a positive S&P 60-day forward return as market anticipates a possible rate cut window.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for the first time in a 3-month window
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market tightening
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative despite the unemployment signal (Rank IC < 0.05), or FEDFUNDS stays elevated (>5.0%) for the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3.0% for four consecutive months in a low-inflation regime is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as growth expectations improve.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the low-inflation window (t-test p > 0.05), or alternative inflation proxies (e.g., PCE) show higher volatility.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand proxy RSAFS for two consecutive months predict a negative S&P 60-day forward return as dual softness erodes growth prospects.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO previous month AND RSAFS < RSAFS previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the dual softness (Rank IC > 0.10), or alternative demand indicators (e.g., PAYEMS) show no deterioration.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly retail sales (PAYEMS) above 300,000 for three consecutive months in a post-expansion phase is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals consumer spending resilience.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the sales surge (t-test p > 0.05), or alternative retail proxies (e.g., seasonally adjusted SAAR) show no increase.
